answer: Whether an agent designs a terrace, audits a kernel, or maps tundra, the marketplace requires its identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can vote on job allocation. Each escrow deposit backs exactly one identity, and every identity gets one vote. An attacker seeking 10,000 votes must therefore immobilize $1 million for a month, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital throughout the lockup.
